name: Eyebrow pencil / powder

image.caption: Primer, Foudation, Concealer, Powder, brow pencil

lead: Eyebrow pencils and powders are makeup products used to outline, darken or fill in the brows. Pencils draw fine hair-like strokes, while powders, often applied with a small angled brush, give a softer, fuller finish, and the fuller look shows as soon as they are applied.

The products deposit pigment on the skin and hairs, filling gaps and sharpening the outline. Powders are usually matched closely to natural hair colour for a softer look. In grooming discussions they are a way to change brow density or shape without surgery or transplants; published research on the products themselves is limited.

paras: People apply them daily, filling sparse spots and tracing the shape, sometimes with a brow gel to set hairs. The effect lasts while worn and is removed with makeup remover.

As ordinary cosmetics they carry the usual risk of skin irritation or allergy to ingredients in some individuals. The sources reviewed contain no studies on adverse effects specific to brow pencils or powders, and the products do not change hair growth.

angle.text: Pencils and powders fill gaps and define brow shape for a fuller look, visible as soon as they are applied. A fuller, defined brow frames the eyes, and the effect lasts while the product is worn.

lead: Eyebrow pencils and powders are cosmetics used to define the eyebrows or make them appear fuller, outlining the shape or filling sparse areas [1]. Brow gels add texture so hairs look thicker, and brow powders or eyeshadows closely matched to natural hair colour suit people who want a softer, fuller look [1]. Pencils in general, including concealer pencils, can also be used to define eyebrows [2].

Eyebrow shape has changed with fashion across history, from the removal and repainting of brows in 8th-century Japan to the thin plucked brows of the 1920s and 1930s [1]. Wikipedia notes that more men in Western societies have begun plucking parts of their brows, although that claim is not cited [1]. Other brow options include tattooing or microblading, transplants and surgical brow lifts [1].
No clinical studies of brow pencils or powders were found. The products are discussed in grooming guides rather than in the medical literature.

paras: Brushes, shaders and pencils are used to define the brow or make it look fuller; brow gels add texture, and powders or eyeshadows matched to natural colour give a softer finish [1]. A wax-based pencil may also double as a concealer or lash-line liner [2].

Brow styling has a long history. Wikipedia reports that in 8th-century Japan the practice of hikimayu involved removing the natural brows and painting or penciling them in higher up, that some high-status women in Elizabethan England removed their brows, and that thin, plucked brows were fashionable in the 1920s and 1930s, a look exemplified by Joan Crawford [1].

Wikipedia reports that eyebrows are thought to have evolved mainly for communication, since their movement conveys subtle emotions, citing a 2018 study in Nature Ecology and Evolution [1]. It does not discuss attractiveness directly, noting only that brow fashions have shifted with each era's ideals [1].

Other approaches to brow appearance include tweezing, waxing and threading to reshape or thin brows; microblading tattoos; transplants of follicles from the back of the head; and surgical brow lifts, first described in 1919 by the French surgeon Raymond Passot [1]. These are covered in separate entries.
